scope: Exact reviewed fep159 maturity row/raw block,standalone EFE capability row,and four theorem-owner names. Existing fixtures remain byte-frozen.

before.invariant: For a full-support two-state belief, its finite KL gap to the invariant law is at most productionRate/decayRate. A specific policy-independent perfect-observation model has EFE equal to the semigroup-evolved gap; that gap is bounded by the explicit squared exponential relaxation factor times the initial chi-square expression. At positive time the supported source-target slice production equals(1-rho)*productionRate/decayRate. Under inverse-epsilon rate scaling, the retained theorem gives, for each positive tolerance, existence of one positive epsilon achieving it; a forall-sufficiently-small-epsilon or Tendsto theorem is not asserted by that declaration.
before.assumption_review: All statements are for the explicit two-state continuous-time semigroup and its scaled one-parameter family; the slice-path identity is the one-slice restriction of the path-thermodynamics production, not a general path-space theorem. The ness_flow import is an orphan-adoption marker with no mathematical dependence.
before.non_vacuity: At the stationary law the gap and production rate both vanish, providing an equality boundary. A full-support nonstationary belief supplies nonzero deviation and current-affinity production for the positive rates, and the explicit rate-scaling envelope gives arbitrarily small attainable gap values at a fixed positive time. The retained declarations do not separately state the full right-limit quantifier.
before.acceptance_probe: warning-free native Lean compile of all nine fep-159 declarations.

after.invariant: For a full-support two-state belief, its finite KL gap to the invariant law is at most productionRate/decayRate. A specific policy-independent perfect-observation model has EFE equal to the semigroup-evolved gap; that gap is bounded by the explicit squared exponential relaxation factor times the initial chi-square expression. At positive time the supported source-target slice production equals(1-rho)*productionRate/decayRate. Under inverse-epsilon rate scaling, the old attainable-scale theorem is preserved. The uniform theorem controls every sufficiently small positive epsilon, and the Tendsto theorem proves the genuine right-hand limit at zero for every fixed positive time and initial finite law.
after.assumption_review: All statements use the explicit two-state continuous-time semigroup and positive rates. The uniform bound and right-hand limit require fixed strictly positive time but permit zero-mass atoms in the initial law. The affinity and slice-path identities retain their explicit full-support premises; the path identity is one-slice, not a general path-space theorem. The ness_flow import remains only an orphan-adoption marker.
after.non_vacuity: A symmetric-rate nonstationary three-quarter/one-quarter belief and a sparse point mass both satisfy the positive-time right limit. The stationary law has exactly zero gap at every positive scale and nonnegative time. At time zero the symmetric point mass retains log 2 at every positive scale, so dropping the positive-time premise is refuted. These controls use the same existing finite probability carrier and public owner.
after.acceptance_probe: Warning-free native Lean compile of all eleven fep-159 declarations, strict importing consumer with five concrete controls, and seven standard-axiom reports for the two public limit proofs and those controls.

before.title: Exact standalone EFE theorems
before.description: The Boltzmann-form control posterior minimizes the expected free energy with the stated uniqueness boundary; the perception-action loop admits an invariant surprisal bound through one controlled-kernel step; Bayesian model reduction never lowers evidence free energy under masked evidence; and the epistemic gain of an EFE time-scale separation is bounded by the log-affinity of its two-state carrier. Each result is a standalone Lean module bridged to its nearest catalogue topic; infinite-horizon, continuous-state, and physical entropy-production identification are not claimed.

after.title: Exact standalone EFE theorems
after.description: The Boltzmann-form control posterior minimizes the expected free energy with the stated uniqueness boundary; the perception-action loop admits an invariant surprisal bound through one controlled-kernel step; Bayesian model reduction never lowers evidence free energy under masked evidence; and the epistemic gain of an EFE time-scale separation is bounded by the log-affinity of its two-state carrier. At each fixed positive time, its inverse-scale family also satisfies a uniform sufficiently-small-scale bound and a genuine right-hand limit at zero; no such limit is claimed at time zero. Each result is a standalone Lean module bridged to its nearest catalogue topic; infinite-horizon, continuous-state, and physical entropy-production identification are not claimed.
